newsitem.title: USA: Arkansas soy harvest stalls in week, corn proceeds.
newsitem.headline: Arkansas soy harvest stalls in week, corn proceeds.

text.p: Harvesting of soybeans was stalled in Arkansas by rains and cold weather in the week ended on September 1 but corn and sorghum harvest progressed, the state agricultural statistics service said.
Soybeans were three percent harvested against two percent a week earlier, nil last year and nil on a five-year average. Soybeans were only five percent mature vs nil y/a, nil avge.
Soybeans were rated 50 percent good to excellent versus 56 percent a week ago, and 32 fair versus 29 last week.

Corn harvest progressed to 33 percent complete from 18 a week ago, 54 last year and 47 on average. Corn condition was rated 70 pct good to excellent, down two percentage points. Aflatoxin problems were reported in some corn fields of Independence County, the report said.
Sorghum was 30 percent harvested against 16 percent last week, 19 last year and 22 avge. Its condition was rated 53 percent good to excellent, up two percentage points.
Rice was six percent harvested, against five last week, six last year and 11 average. The crop was rated 81 percent good to excellent, unchanged from last week.
Cotton continued to suffer from bollworm and weevil in some counties but the crop overall was rated 74 percent good to excellent, up three points in the week.
Cotton opening bolls 37 pct vs 40 y/a, 21 avge.
Livestock were rated in good condition across the state.
